body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: b0ea9f8bc4e1d02d578cbfefff04c2b3e21be992 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is a test-only change: two new UI tests plus one decision file. Nothing in product behaviour, a post, a toolpath or a golden is touched. It merges cleanly with current `main` (`392980120`, trial merge clean) and the touched modules pass with clippy clean.

## What looks good
- The two new tests drive the real controls: clicks on the Browser view-menu checkbox by its accessible label, and a pointer click on the actual viewport axes button at its live HUD anchor (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/display_menu.rs:113-131`, `view_names.rs:47-69`).
- Each test checks the three things the issue asks: axes flip on->off, Grid stays on, and the production `ground_grid_lines` result stays nonempty (#3322).
- No new binary or test-only seam, no production change. The new tests join the existing directory suite. The decision file `docs/decisions/3377-grid-axes-switch-tests.md` follows the repo format.
- README format for the decision file matches. Conventional commit subject. Body ends with `Fixes #3377` and carries a `Changelog: none (test-only)` line.
- The negative control the author describes is sound by inspection: `ground_grid_lines` reads only `show_grid` (crates/ui/src/interact.rs:863-866), so a guard on `show_world_axes` would fail the final assertion. I did not re-run the control. Both new tests pass in my run.

## Results merged with main (local)
- Trial merge of the PR with `origin/main` at `392980120` (trial merge, no commits made): went well, no conflicts. `git diff origin/main` of the merged tree is the 3 PR files only.
- Branch: the PR head at `b0ea9f8bc`. The body base named `231b17d8b`; `main` has since moved. Tests run in the merged tree.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib leaves_the_ground_grid_visible`: both new tests pass (2/2).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib display_menu`: 9 passed, 0 failed (includes the new viewport-axes test).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib view_names`: 3 passed, 0 failed (includes the new Browser-axes test).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passes, no warnings.
- No snapshot PNG, golden, `crates/ui/tests/snapshots/` or `CHANGELOG.md` change. No `build.rs`, `scripts/`, `.github/`, `Cargo.toml`, `.cargo/` or `xtask/` change. This is a read-and-build path, not "read, not built".
- The runner (`pr-test.yml`) is not used here: the author is not a collaborator with push access (outside PR), so the workflow would refuse it. Local build as instructed.

## Targeted tests (step 5)
- Example catalog suites: none - the diff touches no post or toolpath, so no `example_catalog*` run.
- P1 targeted heavy step: not applicable - this is a P7 test-only change, not a post/toolpath/collision change; not under the safety floor.
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`): **not run** - a time-boxed release build of `camcraft-motion`/`camcraft-app` did not complete on this shared machine in the review time box (it was cancelled after the foreground build was backgrounded past the budget). This is not a finding: the diff reaches no motion, app, post or heavy code, so the light lane does not verify anything this PR changes. The PR body records the author's own green light-lane run on this head, with all five selected steps and 11 twins named. If a full light run is wanted before merge, it can be run locally with `cargo xtask gate light`.

## Requested before merge
None.

## Questions / notes
- The PR body claims a quick-gate summary on the committed head; the local run is on the merged tree, which is the right comparison. Nothing here blocks the merge.
- The two modules now contain 11 tests, up from 9, which is what the body says (9 pre-existing, 11 after). The Display module has 8 tests (1 new + 7 existing); the run shows 9 passing under the `display_menu` filter, matching the page-layout test whose name contains "display_menu" - no discrepancy.
- Browser axes checkbox (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/browser_pane.rs:129`) is a plain checkbox that does not persist view state, unlike the Display menu. That is production behaviour, not a defect; the test asserts only the grid and axes state, so the test may not catch a regression that later persists the axes off into the view file. Worth a word if the maintainer wants the checkbox to persist like the Display menu; not blocking.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
